Gold
gōld
n. (the most precious metal; the metal of the holy place; rendering Hebrew zahab, Greek chrusos)
From the Saxon gold, related to gelo, yellow. Hebrew zahab is from a root meaning to shimmer or be yellow, and it is the first metal named in Scripture — the gold of Havilah is called good in Genesis 2, before the fall and before any commerce in it.

Biblical Definition

Gold is the metal of the holy place. The ark, the mercy seat, the table, the candlestick, and the altar of incense are gold or overlaid with it, while the outer court is brass, so that the metals mark increasing nearness to God. “And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold” (Exodus 25:17) — the place where the blood was sprinkled and where God promised to meet with Moses is the purest metal in the sanctuary. Scripture consistently ranks gold below things that cannot be mined. Proverbs sets character above it: “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold” (Proverbs 22:1). Peter sets faith above it: the trial of your faith is “much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire” (1 Peter 1:7) — gold perishes, and tested faith does not. Job, in the middle of unexplained suffering, makes gold the figure of what God is doing to him: “when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold” (Job 23:10). And the last vision reduces gold to paving: in the city, “the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass” (Revelation 21:21) — what men kill for is walked on there.

Webster 1828 Definition

The most precious metal, and in the tabernacle the metal of the holy place and the mercy seat. Scripture consistently ranks a good name, tried faith, and the words of God above it.

expand to see more

GOLD, n. [Sax. gold.] A precious metal of a bright yellow color, the most ductile and malleable of all metals, and of great weight.

2. Money; riches; wealth; as, the love of gold.

3. Something pleasing or valuable; as, a heart of gold.

4. In the tabernacle, the metal of the ark, the mercy seat, the table, and the candlestick.

5. In Scripture, a figure of tried faith; as, when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold, Job 23.

Key Scripture

Exodus 25:17 — "And thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold: two cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof."

1 Peter 1:7 — "That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ:"

Job 23:10 — "But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold."

Revelation 21:21 — "And the twelve gates were twelve pearls; every several gate was of one pearl: and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass."

Modern Corruption

Gold remains the standard of value, and Scripture agrees it is precious while insisting it perishes. The consistent biblical move is to name something better — a good name, tried faith, the words of God.

expand to see more

Two familiar errors attach to this metal. The first is the love of it, which Paul calls the root of all evil — not money itself, but the love of money, a distinction popular misquotation regularly loses. The second is the ascetic overcorrection that treats wealth as inherently sinful, which the tabernacle refutes: God commanded a great deal of gold for his sanctuary, and Abraham, Job, and Joseph of Arimathaea were wealthy men. Gold is a good creature; the question is always what a man does with it and what he thinks it can buy.

The principle to recover is the ranking Scripture keeps making. Proverbs 22:1 puts a good name above it, Psalm 19 puts the judgments of the LORD above much fine gold, and 1 Peter 1:7 puts tested faith above it on the specific ground that gold perishes and faith does not. Revelation 21:21 completes the argument with an image rather than a proposition: in the city gold is paving material. Nothing in Scripture despises gold, and nothing in Scripture is impressed by it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew zahab is gold, from a root of shimmering; paz is fine or refined gold, and kethem is pure gold. Greek chrusos is gold and chrusion a golden article or coin.

expand to see more

Hebrew zahab (H2091) — gold; the metal of the ark, the mercy seat, and the holy place furniture.

Hebrew paz (H6337) — fine gold, refined gold; more to be desired than much fine gold, Psalm 19:10.

Hebrew kethem (H3800) — pure gold; used in Job and the Song for what is most precious.

Greek chrusos (G5557) — gold; the gift of the wise men and the paving of the city.

Greek chrusion (G5553) — a golden article, gold coin; I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire.

Usage

"Of the mercy seat where God met with Moses: thou shalt make a mercy seat of pure gold (Exodus 25:17)."

"Of tried faith ranked above it: much more precious than of gold that perisheth (1 Peter 1:7)."

"Of its final status in the city: the street of the city was pure gold (Revelation 21:21)."
